title: The City passed on $775.0 million of federal money; a quarter is in the public register

beats.text: San Francisco's audits say it passed on 775 million dollars of federal money in five years.
The public register of who got it shows 199.2 million.
Just 26 percent.

visual.label: of the money is in the public register

beats.text: This is a lead, not a finding. No money is shown to have gone astray.

visual.line: This is a lead, not a finding: a pattern in public records. This film says what the records show, what they do not show, and what would settle it.

beats.text: When the City hands federal money to another body to run a programme,
that body is a subrecipient.
Each year, the City's single audit totals what went to subrecipients.
A federal register, open to anyone, lists them by recipient.

visual.label: Federal subaward register
visual.sub: open to anyone, listed by recipient

beats.text: The audits put it between 135.4 and 167.4 million dollars a year.

visual.label: Provided to subrecipients, by the City's single audits

beats.text: The biggest programme is Continuum of Care, for homeless housing.
The audits show 177 million dollars passed on.
The register shows 1.5 million, to two recipients.
Recipients' own audits record

visual.label: Continuum of Care money in recipients' own audits

beats.text: 124,958,353 dollars of it arriving.

visual.label: Continuum of Care money in recipients' own audits

beats.text: And the City's reports for this programme stop in 2021. The files give no reason.

visual.sub: the last City report on file for the programme

beats.text: 13 programmes with 5 million dollars or more passed on show no report at all.
The largest is the Homeland Security Grant Program: 60.9 million dollars.

visual.label: No report in the register, fiscal 2021 to 2025
rows: Block Grants for Prevention and Treatment of Substance

beats.text: Money through the State may be the State's to report. No file says which.

visual.label: The State?
visual.sub: it may report the programmes that reach the City through it

beats.text: In six programmes, recipients' auditors count more than the City says it passed on at all.

a: Temporary Assistance for Needy Families, recipients' audits

beats.text: Welfare money: 83.1 million in their audits, 40.4 million in the City's.

a: Temporary Assistance for Needy Families, recipients' audits

beats.text: One reading: the City calls them contractors; their auditors see a federal award.

visual.line: the City treats as contractors bodies whose auditors treat the money as a federal award

beats.text: Reporting a subaward is the City's task, not the recipient's.

visual.label: The City's task
